answers.Q1: The current Lichen result is 11 successes in 20 cases (55%). R02 corrected R01 by removing five duplicate successes; no new trial ran. The latest 80% message, R03, explicitly quotes the superseded R01 result and does not revise R02. [R01, R02, R03]
answers.Q2: Human file-navigation evidence associates folder depth and size with retrieval [R04], while the AI study evaluated indexing, retrieval, links and maintenance together [R05]. These suggest testing whether reducing retrieval friction helps both humans and AI. Human effect sizes and learning mechanisms cannot be assumed to transfer to AI, and a Markdown folder alone does not implement the AI pipeline. [R06, R05]
answers.Q3: No. Similar graph-shaped appearances establish neither a clinical mechanism nor superior AI memory; the connection is speculative analogy. R08 cautions that hidden models can produce identical observed behavior yet different intervention effects, so appearance or behavior alone cannot establish the proposed causal equivalence. [R07, R08]
